name: Pawn Camp
blurb: Meet the six pieces one at a time, then play your first whole game.
who: For anyone who has never played. No reading needed.

steps.text: This is the board. Every square has a name.
A letter goes across. A number goes up.

steps.ask: Tap the square d5.
steps.hint: Find the letter d along the bottom. Then count up to 5.
steps.why: That is d5. Letter first, then number.

steps.ask: Now tap h1.
steps.hint: h is the last letter. 1 is the bottom row.
steps.why: h1 is the corner nearest White. It is a light square.

steps.ask: Which corner square is on your right when you are White?
steps.why: White on the right. The light square goes in the right corner.

steps.text: Now the pieces can move in.
You can read the board now.

lessons.name: The Rook
lessons.big: Straight lines, as far as it likes.

steps.text: This is a rook. It is the castle tower.

steps.cap: A rook runs in straight lines. Up, down, left and right.

steps.ask: Move the rook to d7.
steps.hint: Straight up the line it is already on.
steps.wrongSay: A rook does not go slanted. Try a straight line.

steps.text: A rook cannot jump. It stops at the first piece.

steps.ask: Tap the far square the rook can reach going up.
steps.hint: It stops where the black pawn is. It can take that pawn.
steps.why: It stops there and takes the pawn. It cannot jump over it.

steps.ask: Collect all three stars. Three moves is the best you can do.

steps.text: Straight lines, every time.

lessons.name: The Bishop
lessons.big: Slanted lines, and it keeps its colour forever.

steps.text: Bishops walk on slants. Never straight.

steps.cap: Every slanted line, as far as it likes.

steps.text: Look at the colour. It never leaves the dark squares.

steps.ask: Send the bishop to g7.
steps.hint: Up and to the right, one slanted line.
steps.wrongSay: A bishop cannot go straight. Follow a slant.

steps.ask: Could this bishop ever reach e4?

choices.text: No, e4 is a light square

steps.why: It started on a dark square, so it can only ever visit dark ones.

steps.ask: How far up and right can it go? Tap the last square.
steps.hint: It stops where the black pawn is standing.
steps.why: It stops at the pawn, and it may take it. It cannot jump over.

steps.ask: Three stars, all on dark squares. Three moves is the best.

steps.text: One colour, forever.

lessons.name: The Queen
lessons.big: A rook and a bishop in one.

steps.text: The queen is a rook and a bishop in one piece.

steps.cap: Straight lines and slanted lines. Twenty-seven squares from here.

steps.ask: Move the queen to g7, the slanted way.
steps.hint: Up and right along the slant, like a bishop.
steps.wrongSay: That is a square, but not g7. Try again.

steps.ask: Tap a square the queen can NOT reach in one move.
steps.hint: Think of the knight's jump. The queen cannot do that.
steps.why: b3 is not on a straight or slanted line from d4. Only a knight jumps like that.

steps.ask: Three stars in three moves. The queen can do it.

steps.text: She is the strongest piece. Look after her.
The queen goes everywhere.

lessons.name: The Knight
lessons.big: Gallop, gallop, step to the side.

steps.text: The knight jumps. Two steps, then one to the side.

steps.cap: Eight places to land. It is the only piece that jumps over others.

steps.ask: Jump the knight to f5.
steps.hint: Two to the right, then one up.
steps.wrongSay: Not that one. Two steps, then one to the side.

steps.text: Every jump lands on the other colour. Dark, light, dark.

steps.ask: Tap all eight pawns this knight can jump to.
steps.hint: There are eight. They make a ring around the knight.
steps.why: Eight jumps, eight pawns. That ring is the knight's whole world.

steps.ask: Gallop to all three stars. Three jumps is the best you can do.

steps.text: Gallop, gallop, step to the side.

lessons.name: The Pawn
lessons.big: Forward one. It eats sideways. It never goes back.

steps.text: Pawns only go forward. They can never turn back.
One step. Or two, but only from its very first square.

steps.cap: But it eats sideways. Forward to walk, slanted to take.

steps.ask: Tap the two pawns this pawn can take.
steps.hint: Not the square in front. The two slanted ones.
steps.why: A pawn walks forward but eats sideways. That catches everybody out once.

steps.ask: Take the pawn on e3.
steps.hint: Slanted, up and to the right.
steps.wrongSay: To take, go slanted. Straight ahead is only for walking.

steps.text: A pawn that reaches the far side turns into a queen.

steps.goal: Eight pawns each. Get one all the way across.

steps.text: The smallest piece, and the one that grows up.

lessons.name: The King
lessons.big: One careful step, and never into danger.

steps.text: The king takes one step. Any direction.

steps.cap: Eight squares around him. Slow, but he can go anywhere.

steps.text: But he may never step where an enemy could take him.

steps.ask: Only two squares are safe. Tap them both.
steps.hint: The black rook watches the whole second row. Stay off it.
steps.why: The rook covers every square on row 2, so the king must stay on row 1.

steps.ask: Could the king step to e2?

choices.text: No, the rook would take him

steps.why: A king may never walk onto a square an enemy piece is watching.

steps.text: Losing the king loses the game. Keep him safe.
One careful step at a time.
Every piece is worth points. Pawn 1. Knight and bishop 3.
Rook 5. Queen 9. The king is worth the whole game.

steps.ask: Which is worth more, a rook or a bishop?
steps.why: A rook is 5 and a bishop is 3. Two whole points.

steps.cap: This knight can take two things. One is worth more.

steps.ask: Take the bigger one.
steps.hint: The rook is 5. The bishop is only 3.
steps.wrongSay: That one is worth less. Look for the rook.

steps.text: A piece nobody is guarding is free. Always look.

steps.ask: Tap the white piece that nobody is guarding.
steps.hint: It is out on its own in the middle.
steps.why: The knight on e5 has no friend near it. Black can just take it.

steps.text: You count like a chess player now.
Check means the king is being attacked right now.
You must answer it at once. There are three ways.

steps.ask: One: run away. Move the king somewhere safe.
steps.hint: Off the bottom row, where the rook cannot reach.
steps.wrongSay: Move the king itself this time.

steps.ask: Two: block it. Put a piece in the way, on c1.
steps.hint: The bishop or the knight can both reach c1.
steps.wrongSay: Get something onto c1, between the rook and the king.

steps.ask: Three: take it. Capture the rook.
steps.hint: The knight can jump to a1.
steps.wrongSay: Something can reach a1 and take the rook.

steps.ask: What if none of the three works?

choices.text: That is checkmate, and the game is over

steps.why: No run, no block, no take. That is checkmate, and we do it next.

steps.text: Run, block, or take.

lessons.name: Checkmate and Stalemate
lessons.big: Trapped is a win. Frozen is a tie.

steps.text: Checkmate is check with no way out. The game ends.

steps.cap: He cannot run, cannot block, cannot take. Checkmate.

steps.text: Now a strange one. This king is not in check at all.

steps.cap: But he has nowhere to go. That is stalemate, and it is a draw.

steps.ask: You are winning easily and you stalemate them. Who wins?
steps.why: Stalemate is a draw however far ahead you were. Always leave them a move.

steps.ask: Your turn. Find the checkmate with the rook.
steps.hint: Along the bottom of their side. Their own pawns trap them.
steps.wrongSay: Close. Look at the row their king is stuck on.

steps.goal: Five positions. One move ends each of them.

steps.text: You can finish a game now.

lessons.name: Castling
lessons.big: The king runs home and the tower shuts the door.

steps.text: Once a game, the king can jump two squares to safety.

steps.cap: The rook hops over him and shuts the door. This is castling.

steps.ask: Castle. Move the king two squares to g1.
steps.hint: Tap the king, then tap g1. The rook follows on its own.

steps.cap: You can go the long way too, over to c1.

steps.ask: Can you castle while you are in check?

choices.text: Yes, it is a good escape

steps.why: Not in check, not through check, not into check. Three nots.

steps.ask: Your rook moved out and came back. Can you still castle with it?
steps.why: The king and that rook must both never have moved. Coming back does not count.

steps.text: Your king has a castle to hide in.

lessons.name: Growing Up, and Sneaking Past
lessons.big: A pawn can become a queen.

steps.text: A pawn that reaches the far side becomes a new piece.

steps.ask: Push the pawn home and make a queen.
steps.hint: One step up. Then pick the queen from the four choices.

steps.text: You could pick a rook, bishop or knight. Almost nobody does.
Now the sneakiest rule in chess.

steps.cap: Their pawn jumped two, straight past yours. You can still catch it.

steps.ask: Catch it. Take slanted, onto the empty square d6.
steps.hint: Move to d6 as if the pawn had only gone one square.
steps.wrongSay: Go to d6. The pawn on d5 comes off anyway.

steps.ask: Can you do that a few moves later instead?
steps.why: Only on the very next move. Miss it and the chance is gone.

steps.text: Two secret moves, both yours.

lessons.name: The Secret Code
lessons.big: Every move has a name you can write down.

steps.text: Every move has a short name you can write down.
The piece letter, then the square. Nf3 is knight to f3.

steps.ask: Play Nf3.
steps.hint: N is the knight. Send it to f3.
steps.wrongSay: N means knight. f3 is the square.

steps.ask: What does Bxe5 mean?
steps.why: The little x means takes. So Bxe5 is bishop takes whatever is on e5.

steps.ask: What is O-O?
steps.why: O-O is castling the short way. O-O-O is the long way.

steps.ask: A move written with a # at the end means what?
steps.why: A + is check. A # is checkmate, and the game stops there.

steps.cap: The shortest game there is. Watch it in the code you just learned.

notes.3: 2. g4 — now two holes in front of the king.

steps.text: You can read chess like a book.

lessons.name: How a Game Ends
lessons.big: Some games end in a handshake.

steps.text: Not every game has a winner. Some end in a handshake.
Stalemate is one. No check, but no move either.

steps.cap: Here is another. A king and one bishop can never checkmate.

steps.ask: King and bishop against a lone king. Who wins?

choices.text: Nobody. There are not enough pieces

steps.why: You cannot checkmate with only a bishop. It is a draw straight away.

steps.ask: Both players just shuffle and nothing changes. Then what?

choices.text: After a while it is a draw

steps.why: The same position three times is a draw. So is fifty moves with no capture.

steps.ask: You are losing badly. Can you offer a draw?

choices.text: Yes, and they can say no

steps.why: Anyone may offer. The other player says yes or no, and play carries on.

steps.text: Now you know every way a game can end.
First, a trap. Somebody will try this on you.

steps.cap: The four-move checkmate. Watch where the queen and bishop point.

notes.5: 3. Qh5 — the queen and the bishop both stare at f7.
notes.6: 3... Nf6 — this does not stop it.
notes.7: 4. Qxf7# — checkmate. Knight School teaches you to beat this.

steps.text: Now a real game. Paris, 1858. Watch White work together.

steps.cap: Every piece has a job. Nobody sits at home.

notes.13: 7. Qb3 — attacking two things at once: f7 and b7.
notes.19: 10. Nxb5 — giving a knight away to open a line.
notes.31: 16. Qb8+ — the queen too. All of it was for this.
notes.33: 17. Rd8# — checkmate, with the last two pieces left.

steps.ask: White gave away a knight, a rook and the queen. Why?

choices.text: To clear the way to checkmate

steps.why: Pieces are only points until the end. Checkmate is worth all of them.

steps.goal: A whole game, all the rules. Win or lose, play it to the end.

steps.text: You played real chess. Knight School is open.
